newsitem.title: UK: Urals steady in quiet Med, Algeria talks start.
newsitem.headline: Urals steady in quiet Med, Algeria talks start.

text.p: Russian Urals crude was assessed steady by Mediterranean crude traders in quiet talk on Monday while most market attention turned to Algerian and Syrian monthly pricing, traders said.
The Russian sour was seen continuing at around a discount of $1.10/$1.15 to international benchmark Dated Brent, its level for the past week.
The Sea Dancer carrying 135,000 tonnes of Urals was sold to a European major late last week at around Dated -$1.12, traders said.

The value was initially reported by the market as Dated Brent -$1.05 and a published report put it at -$1.20. But both figures were later denied by the buyer, who said the private and confidential value was between $1.10 and $1.15. The material is destined mostly for the major's refining system, traders said.
"Until I see a genuine end-user buying I will continue to put Urals at -$1.10/-$1.15," a trader said.
The Matilda carrying one million barrels of Urals loading end-June was offered out on Monday without a number attached.
Demand remains patchy as buyers hang back in the hope of cheaper numbers when Iraqi exports resume.

Talks started in London meanwhile on the pricing for July of Algeria's Saharan Blend, with Sonatrach reportedly putting the value in the region of 40 to 50 cents above Dated Brent and lifters talking in the 30s.
"We see it in the 30s and Sonatrach in the 40s. We'll probably end up in the high 30s," one trader said.
In June Saharan was priced at Dated +60/62 cents.
Traders are also awaiting telexes due imminently on July pricing from Syrian state oil company Sytrol.
Like Urals, Syrian Light is seen benefiting from the uncertainty over the timing of fresh Iraqi exports under the second 180-day period of the "oil for food" programme, traders said.

"For sure there will be an increase (in the Syrian price)," one trader said. "It's an uncertain market. It's a good time for sellers and with the unknown Iraqi factor it's justified to put up the offer."
Syrian light was Dated -77 cents in June, while Souedie was fixed at Dated -$4.40.
On the West African market one trader said the Brent Dubai spread had widened because of talk that large amounts of unsold Nigerian barrels were again moving to Asia.

No details or confirmation were available however, and a recent Asian large volume buyer of Cabinda said it was not in the market on Monday. The buyer assessed the grade at slightly cheaper than a $1 discount to Dated Brent.
A part cargo of Forcados aboard a VLCC was sold on a cif basis late last week to the United States loading Jun 18-21 at a price equivalent on a fob basis to Dated -10 cents.
A Forcados loading July 5-6 moved at eight cents over Dated on Thursday.
Remaining June West African barrels include a Bonny Light VLCC and three Qua Iboes. Bonny Light was assessed at a premium of about 25 to 35 cents over Dated Brent, with Qua Iboe at about 20/30 cents.
-- William Maclean London newsroom +44 171 542 7646
